newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- T-bond vols little changed, Aug calls bid.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- T-bond vols little changed, Aug calls bid.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were generally little changed, although the soon-expiring August contracts saw strong buying interest, dealers said.

A departure from the 114-area in September T-bond futures kept upward pressure on volatilities, but the advance on the whole was slow enough for the options market to catch up without causing a run on volatilities, they said.
"Perhaps this would have been viewed as a breakout yesterday...but obviously volatilities are still pretty low," said a brokerage firm trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
Implied volatility for September T-bond futures options was barely changed at around 8.1 percent.
Most of the largest trades were in August options, which expire on Friday, and the 114 and 115 calls were particularly in demand.

A U.S. bank was said to have bought 15,000 contracts of August 115 calls just before the bond market's rally went into full swing. The bank was also seen buying 5,000 contracts of slightly out-of-the-money August 110 calls in 10-year T-note futures options.

The 115 T-bond calls, which at Tuesday's closing seemed hopelessly out-of-the-money with delta of about 11, have now turned into a viable high-gamma option, traders said. Shortly before the close, with September T-bonds at 114-23/32, the 115 calls had delta of about 35.
Short-dated at-the-money options have high gamma, which provides quick premium acceleration, although they are vulnerable to time decay.
Buying was seen even in the 116 strike, which was still deep out-of-the-money. The 116s, however, were seen bought as a cheap upside hedge rather than for speculative gamma play.
September futures climbed past Friday's 114-15/32 to touch a high of 114-27/32, up nearly a full point on the day, in a rally triggered by a friendly June consumer price index.
Both the overall CPI and the core rate, excluding food and energy, rose 0.1 percent in June, compared with average estimates of a 0.2 percent gain in both.

Traders were awaiting next week's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan. Greenspan was also due to testify before a House subcommittee hearing on the Financial Services Competition Act at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT on Thursday.

Eurodollar futures were slightly firmer on the day, but the December contract failed to rise above last week's 94.090 high, reinforcing perception that futures expiring in the next few quarters would stay range-bound near term, gravitating toward the cash rate, a brokerage trader said.
Implied volatility for December Eurodollar futures options was flat at about 9.4 percent, while the March volatility stood at 11.2 percent.
